heading: Jurisdiction and referenced codes
text: BCP 2021 treats referenced codes as requirements to the extent specified by the code. For plumbing, the IPC applies unless the Authority Having Jurisdiction does not require it. Therefore AHJ should be optional in PumpDesign AI, while the project jurisdiction and applicable code basis remain explicit.

heading: Scope
text: IPC Chapter 6 governs design and installation of building water-supply systems, including hot and cold water and individual water-supply systems. It also addresses materials, installation, hot-water systems, potable-water protection and temperature-control devices.

heading: Applicability
text: IPC Appendix E is an optional appendix unless the adopting ordinance specifically references it. PumpDesign AI must therefore record whether this sizing method is actually applicable rather than treating Appendix E as universally mandatory.

heading: Hydraulic sizing basis
text: Appendix E describes water-piping sizing using available source pressure, elevation/head changes, friction losses and required fixture flow. It also recognizes other good-engineering-practice sizing methods when accepted by the code official.

heading: Pressure and elevation
text: For a building water system, elevation between the supply source and the highest outlet consumes available pressure. The sizing workflow must therefore include elevation head and the required pressure at the critical outlet rather than sizing only from flow.

heading: Pipe sizing workflow
text: A sound pipe-sizing workflow identifies the system type, fluid properties, temperature and pressure conditions, loads/flows, pipe segments, equivalent lengths and losses. PumpDesign AI should use this sequence when the design flow is known or calculated.

heading: Service-water diversity
text: Service-water systems generally should not be sized by assuming every fixture operates simultaneously. Probable simultaneous demand/diversity is a key design issue when the designer has not supplied a design flow.

heading: Hydraulic methods
text: Darcy-Weisbach is a general hydraulic method for pressure-drop calculations. Hazen-Williams is an empirical method commonly used for water piping, but its roughness coefficient should be tied to appropriate pipe conditions and should not be blindly transferred across materials, diameters, velocities or viscosities.

heading: Materials and manufacturer data
text: Pipe material selection must consider pressure, temperature, chemical compatibility, joining and applicable code requirements. Manufacturer literature can supply dimensions and pressure-drop information; actual internal diameter should be used in hydraulic calculations.

heading: Water hammer
text: Rapid stopping of moving water can create large transient pressure rises. Where a design includes rapid-closing valves, long runs, high velocities or sensitive equipment, water-hammer evaluation should be considered rather than ignored.

heading: Hot-water design inputs
text: Hot-water system design depends on flow rate, temperature, total flow over time, operating pressure, delivery time and water quality. Equipment sizing and piping design should be considered together.

heading: Hot-water pipe sizing
text: Hot-water supply piping is hydraulically sized using the same basic pressure-drop principles as cold-water piping, while hot-water demand depends on establishment type, occupancy and time of day. The design should meet peak demand with acceptable pressure loss without unnecessary oversizing.

heading: Pressure differential
text: Hot and cold water piping should be designed to control pressure differential at mixed-water fixtures. Pressure losses through heaters and anti-scald/pressure-compensating devices should be included where applicable.
